x: The sealed handicap went to Len Coleman, who shows improvement every time out, and will be with the leaders before long. Earle claimed second award, and Bill Snell the third prize.

Bill Snell came through well over the last three miles to complete our team and ensure third place for the Club. Our next man to finish was Stan Goold (31st), followed by a very promising newcomer, Syd English (32nd).
Brunning progresses steadily and will perform better over the longer distances. Frank Jarvis won the sealed handicap, and our old friend, Bill Snell, worked his way into second place.
Our handicap was won by Bill Snell with 8 min. 45 sec. allowance. The Handicapper himself was second, and we were all glad to see our persevering Bill Brunning take third prize.
Roberts led the "Bels." home, closely followed by Bill Snell, Jack Bidgood and Bob Readman. Good packing, but not quite near enough to the front.

Bill Snell and Arthur Beales, one of our youngest members, are among the latest to be called up for duty with the Services. Walkers will be pleased to know that Bill Snell, now in Ack Ack Beer Beer down Aberystwyth way, is well and cheery. He aired his walking shoes and a Belgrave Club vest within two days of becoming a soldier, which can't be far short of a world's record!
Jack Shields, in the R.A.F. in Buckinghamshire, says " There is very little opportunity for running here." Bill Snell.—On his way overseas, and who has taken his Belgrave togs with him.
Bill Snell, now in the Middle East, "near a town famous in Biblical history": through miles of orange and lemon groves. Stopped at a " place " where we had eggs and onions twice a day!

Bill Snell, in the M.E., says he and "Charlie Churcher seem to be chasing one another but never meeting. But one fine morning saw Jack Flower, complete in claret and gold, trying out his spikes in the sand.
Jack Flower, now a Captain, writes from the M.E.F. that he has met Bill Snell whilst doing a spot of training on the sand. Sends his regards and best wishes to all his old team-mates.

Bill Snell is very busy in the Middle East, even when "off duty," as his mates have discovered that Bill is a tailor. He sends his congratulations to all the boys who are helping to keep Belgrave to the fore, and to everybody he sends his best wishes.

Jack Watts, another from Eastleigh (yes, the runners have heard about Eastleigh now, Jack) is now in Italy. Bill Snell is on the move again, and is on the trail of Charlie Churcher. These two have often missed seeing each other by a narrow margin.

We have much pleasure in acknowledging Christmas Greetings from: Charlie Churcher (M.E.F.), Alf Harley (C.M.F.), Bill Snell (M.E.F.), Frank Elson (Holland), Charlie Smart (B.L.A.), Dick Towndrow (B.L.A.), Norman Graves (B.L.A), George Durrant (S.E.A.C.), Wally Ives (India), Frank Webb (S.
Bill Snell has been transferred from A.A. to R.A.S.C. He narrowly missed seeing Charlie Churcher recently.
Frank King enjoyed a welcome leave at home this summer, but had to return to Italy. Bill Snell, very busy in an office job with no P.T. The roads are very bad and over mountains, and it is very hot.
Bill Snell is now back from overseas and has already been on the road. Alby Bird, with his wife and youngster, were welcome spectators at the Club Championship Meeting.
